example.summary: The first-run atomic setup transaction: handler setup_complete in apps/api/api/setup.py (21 lines, async, returns MeResponse, status 200) gated by get_auth_context, fed by ONE screen hook (useCompleteSetup, rendered SetupRoute→SetupScreen), fanning out to 29 functions 5 deep that read 13 tables and write 11 of them across 5 entities (auth + settings·allergen·pantry·legal-consent), consuming SetupCompleteRequest (6 nested inputs) and returning MeResponse (6 cols, 5 nested summaries); 26 api test cases all pass, 27 test journeys, 1 curated workflow (Initial setup, step 2 of 4, tier 1); no commit in the 30-commit window, not in flight, no flag wall, no docstring, homing verdict stay.

coverage_note: The feed is a static map with no runtime signal at all: no latency, throughput, error rate, request volume, timeouts, retries, payload sizes, or who-calls-in-production for any endpoint. Status is the declared SUCCESS code only (det.status '200' / HTTP_201_CREATED …); the error statuses a handler raises (400/401/409/422 that the bench's own test names cite — test_setup_complete_missing_key_400, _without_consent_409, _blank_name_422) are nowhere as data, only in prose (det.doc, 36/81) or in test-case names. Test state is uniform (326/326 pass, 100% corpus api) so it separates nothing today, and web/e2e coverage arrives as a count string ('15 case(s)') not as named cases. The request body schema is not marked as such — 'touches' does not distinguish request from response, so request-side is inferred from det.gsig 'body:' (35/81) and the lone 'consumes' edge; stats.consumes says 70 while only 1 consumes edge exists, so that stat counts something the edges do not carry. Auth is nearly uniform (79/81 gated by get_auth_context or its query twin) and app-level middleware (CORS · Idempotency · RateLimit) is never tied to an endpoint (gated_by 0) — permissions/roles per endpoint are absent. Cross-file call hops are inferred-by-design (233/427 fn_edges inferred; graft calls 446 inferred · 0 extracted), so behind.fns (29) and the levels BFS (25) disagree by the graft-only edges — a floor, not a census. det.exported and det.usage.api are constant across all endpoints. Commits cover only 30 commits over 11 days (22/81 touched) and the seeded sim is at rest (every pieces[] empty, no endpoint id present), so change pressure and in-flight state are absent for 59/81 and 81/81 respectively. levels.pressure is {} feed-wide. Idempotency, transactionality and rate limits are visible only indirectly (IdempotencyKey read+write in access.ops, access.commits true) — never as a property. Nothing says whether an endpoint is deprecated, versioned, public vs internal, or its expected caller cadence.

library_laws: THE MOTION CONTRACT (binding on anything that moves): 1 replayable — every animation carries its own Replay control, a one-shot that finished before the reader arrived is a blank card; 2 pausable — a global Motion: Playing/Paused in the cog panel wired to CSS `:root[data-motion="off"]` → animation-play-state:paused AND SMIL svg.pauseAnimations(); 3 reduced-motion safe — under prefers-reduced-motion every element renders its FINISHED state (bars full, traces written, nothing moving), never a start state or an empty frame. Registered via window.FXREPLAY[slug]=build; verified by gabe-artifact tools/verify-motion.mjs (fingerprints transforms/dash/opacity/colour at uneven sample gaps; SKIP on a page that should move = failure). Field-side twin: the station freezes ALL fleets/transports/pulses on camera drag (#freezeDragBtn :1047) and during layout settle (__uniFreezeForSettle).

Ambient/looping motion carries a legible position in time (a ruled belt under a fixed NOW cursor, a ticking label) or it is decoration (visual-grammar.md 'Ambient motion says WHEN'; Timeline conveyor card). Reactive motion (hover/selection) still answers the cog pause, spacebar and reduced-motion (interaction-hooks.md).

THE HONEST-EMPTY LAW: empty · unmeasured · absent are DRAWN states, never blanks and never zero. Four availability states — LIT (a value) · BLANK (wrong question, e.g. BEHIND on a model) · GREY (no answer, CALLERS 0) · HATCHED (never measured — TABLES on every endpoint until F6, TESTED on all 1,078 fe pieces) — each a different next move (docs/design/workflow-panel/README.md:92-93, CONSOLE-MAP.md 'a fourth availability state'); slot tones live/none/unmeas (FIELD-TABLE.md, _lab-fn-layouts.js); gabe-imagine's four actor states running · ghost(dashed) · unpowered(amber) · broken(red), every state used legended beside the thing it colours (SKILL.md P2); the station's Sources/STARS rows and journeys are honest-empty on failure (gabe-universe.html :2725, :5978). Corollary: 'measured zero' ≠ 'never measured' (F2/F6: tests:0 hardcoded reads as untested; a check that always fires is non-evidence). Corollary: a slot that has never carried a value is dead, cut it (dispatch: 16 kinds, 0 values — FIELD-TABLE.md finding 2).

LEGEND = THE ACTUAL GLYPH: the legend cell reuses the very draw function the 3D badge uses (__badgeGlyph :4221 — change a glyph HERE and both move together); wire samples render the real SVG dasharray from DASHMAP (:2201, :3894 — CSS border-style cannot draw 'sparse', so a sample can never lie); legend thumbnails rotate the actual 3D asset through the one shared renderer (legThumb/palR :6128-6133; __uniAssets :6290); every legend row carries a drawn example chip or '—'; words only on hover (:2945, :3825 'glyphs, not words'). wells.label: Data footprint
wells.question: If I call this, what changes — which tables, how far outside its own house — and does the write actually land?
wells.plain: Every table the handler's chain reads or writes (c4-graph.js node .access.ops, rw r|w; the reads_from / writes_to l2 + cross edges), whether the chain commits (.access.commits), and how many of those tables belong to other entities.
wells.why: The first fork before any other reading: read-only is safe to poke, a mutation needs transaction and owner thinking. On the bench 24 ops = 13 r + 11 w over 13 tables, .access.commits true, 8 tables foreign (settings 5 r+w · allergen · pantry · legal-consent r only) — so a change needs four other entities' owners in the review and a bad call leaves landed rows behind. Inverting the reads_from edges (verified on c4-graph.js): 30 other endpoints read the 11 tables this one writes and 6 other endpoints also write them. Feed-wide 79/81 carry ops, 43/81 write, 40/81 cross an entity boundary on data.

wells.label: Who counts on it
wells.question: Who fires this — which screen through which hook, does anything inside the app call it — and which user story stalls, at which step, if it breaks?
wells.plain: The frontend file and hook whose fetch names this endpoint (c4-graph.js cross_edges kind=bridge, export = the hook) climbed to its route through fe.edges renders / uses-hook; internal callers (node .det.usage.internal — levels.json has no fn→handler edge, handlers are roots); and the curated workflow steps that name it (workflows.js steps[]).
wells.why: Tells you who breaks and what to test: on the bench exactly one path — useCompleteSetup (hrole fetcher, cache true, wsites 1) ← SetupScreen ← SetupRoute — no internal caller (.det.usage.internal 0, calls-in 0 feed-wide), and step 2 of 4 in 'Initial setup — first run' (workflows.js, level 1 Orientation), so a regression strands every new account before GET /me ever runs. 28/81 endpoints have no screen and 39/81 sit in no story, so presence is itself the signal; nothing says who calls it in production (coverage_note).
evidence: fe render chain behind the bridge
bridge (web → endpoint, via fetch, export = hook)
fe uses-hook / renders (fe.edges upstream of the bridging hook)
workflow step (workflows.js steps[] naming the label)

wells.label: Response
wells.question: What comes back when it works — which shape, how deep, with what status, all at once or as a stream — and who else speaks that same shape?
wells.plain: The named response schema (c4-graph.js node .resp = .det.payload.schema, .det.payload.n top-level fields, .det.sig.returns), the declared success status (.det.status), whether delivery is a stream (.stream), the sub-shapes one hop down (nests edges), whether it mirrors a table (serializes edges), and the entity that owns the class (levels.json use_edges). The verb in .label + status + commits together say what kind of door it is.
wells.why: Tells the screen what to unpack and how errors arrive (statuses vs events on a stream), and whether editing the shape is editing someone else's contract: MeResponse (6 cols, 5 nested summaries, serializes no table) is owned by progression and is the .resp of three endpoints (verified on c4-graph.js: GET /me, POST /setup/complete, POST /_e2e/seed), so a renamed field lands in GET /me and the e2e seed at once. The bench is a one-shot 200 transaction; the contrast GET /recipe-creation/gustify/stream (.stream true) delivers in pieces with errors as events — the one endpoint fact that IS a time behaviour. 14/81 return no named schema.
evidence: nests (schema → schema, one hop off the endpoint's schemas)
serializes (schema → model, one hop, conf inferred)

wells.label: Request
wells.question: What do I have to send — which body type, how much of it must be assembled before it validates, and which function actually reads it?
wells.plain: The request body type, readable only in the clipped signature (c4-graph.js node .det.gsig 'body:'), the sub-shapes it nests one hop down (nests edges), and the chain function that consumes it (levels.json schema_edges). 'touches' edges never say request vs response, and the explicit consumes edge is drawn 1/81 while stats.consumes says 70.
wells.why: Decides whether a new screen can call it and whether a contract change breaks the one hook that fetches it: SetupCompleteRequest nests 6 inputs the caller assembles (DietaryProfileInput, HouseholdFormatInput, NotificationPreferencesInput, PrivacyPermissions…, Exploration…, UserFormat…), and a 400/422 is a shape failure in one of those six; the handler never touches the schema — services/setup.py#complete_setup does (levels.json schema_edges) — so the edit site is two files from the route. Request side is inferred from gsig (35/81 carry 'body:'), a words-dependency until consumes is emitted.
evidence: nests (schema → schema, one hop off the endpoint's schemas)

wells.label: Chain behind the handler
wells.question: How much work sits behind the handler, how deep does it go, where do the reads and writes actually happen — and which hops is the map only guessing at?
wells.plain: The transitive call tree under the handler (c4-graph.js node .behind.fns / .depth / .names / .names_more / .truncated; levels.json fn_edges walked from fn_nodes '<det.file>#<fn>' with conf extracted|inferred per hop), the handler's own size (.det.sig.lines, .det.file:flines) and its distance to the first write (levels.json fn_nodes d2w).
wells.why: Prices the reading before an edit and picks the first file to open in an incident: 29 fns 5 deep (feed range 0–135 / 0–7) behind a 21-line handler with 3 direct out-edges — the handler is a delegate; complete_setup fans to 15 callees at layer 2 (_upsert_* ×5, _stamp_completion, _subscription_block) where the writes live (handler fn_node d2w 1, access absent). Read services/setup.py next, not the route. The two counts disagree (behind 29 vs the levels BFS 25 in layers [3,16,5,1]) by graft-only inferred edges — 233/427 fn_edges inferred — a floor not a census, so inferred hops are where the picture may be lying.
evidence: calls (handler fn → callee, levels fn_edges, direct)

wells.label: Gate
wells.question: Who can turn this request away before my code runs — which dependency, which flag, which app-level middleware — and who is the door for?
wells.plain: The FastAPI dependencies injected into the handler (c4-graph.js node .middleware[], gate:true = the one that can refuse, fn = where it lives; levels.json fn_edges rel=depends), the feature flags that wall it (.flags[] and the walls edges with on / on_fail), and the ASGI layer (3 app-middleware nodes — CORS · Idempotency · RateLimit — tied to no endpoint, stats.app_middleware.gated_by 0).
wells.why: Decides how a test or a new caller authenticates, whether you can curl it locally, and in an incident whether the hunt is auth or handler. Nearly uniform — 79/81 gated by get_auth_context (stats.gate_endpoints 79) — so the informative cases are the exceptions: the 2 ungated (BOOT lifespan, GET /healthz), the query-string twin get_auth_context_from_query on the stream, and the 3 walled endpoints (stream: RECIPE_CREATION_ENABLED on:'off' on_fail:'HTTPException'). The bench is the standard case: one gate, no wall. Rate-limit / idempotency per endpoint is unmeasured, and roles, permissions, public-vs-internal and audience are absent entirely — draw those as unknown, not absent.
evidence: depends (handler fn → dependency fn, levels fn_edges)

wells.label: Error contract
wells.question: What can go wrong — which error statuses does it raise (400/401/409/422), and where is that written down?
wells.plain: The failure half of the response. The feed carries only the declared success code (c4-graph.js node .det.status); the errors a handler raises exist nowhere as data — only in prose (.det.doc, 36/81, absent on the bench) or inside test-case names (.det.cases[].name: test_setup_complete_missing_key_400_C1048, _blank_name_422_C1051, _too_many_allergens_422_C1052, _without_consent_409_C1055).
wells.why: The one thing a caller must know before wiring a client, and the branch an incident responder maps a status to before opening a file; a change that adds a failure mode has no field to land in. Half-blind by design: the test-named statuses are the known branches, everything else is an unmeasured slot, so an endpoint with no doc and no error-named test must show the gap rather than a clean door.

wells.label: Test cover
wells.question: What proves this works today, from which corpus, and which walks would go red if I broke it — including the ones I can't see by name?
wells.plain: The test cases whose path touches the endpoint (c4-graph.js node .det.cases[] cid / corpus / name / state), the non-api corpora that reach it as a count string only (.det.case_files[] — web '15 case(s)', never named), and the test journeys through it with component count and the entities they cross (.det.test_journeys[] + test_journeys_more).
wells.why: Decides whether to refactor on green or write a case first, and which suites to run: 26 api cases (setup-named C1048–C1052, C1055–C1057, C389–C392 plus cross-entity C218 / C250 / C251 / C555…), 15 unnamed web cases, 27 journeys of 17–27 components spanning 4–5 entities — a red here fires in three corpora and the web one cannot be targeted from the feed. State is 326/326 pass, 100% corpus api, so today only COUNT separates endpoints (range 0–27); colour carries nothing until a run flips it.

wells.label: Afterwards
wells.question: Once the handler returns or dies, what happens next — where does the result go, does anything keep running, and does a retry replay cleanly or double-write?
wells.plain: The consequences past the response: the fetching hook's cache (c4-graph.js fe piece, cache true), the next step of the story (workflows.js steps[]), a commit landing (node .access.commits), a queue or worker (.access.sinks; levels.json fn_edges rel=dispatches), a stream that keeps delivering (.stream), an internal caller (.det.usage.internal), and the replay contract — never a property, visible only as IdempotencyKey read + written in .access.ops and in test names (_replay_identical_count_one_C1050, _reject_then_accept_retry_same_key_200_C1057, _replay_is_idempotent_no_duplicate_C392).
wells.why: Closes the loop for a change and bounds an incident to the request: the cache fills on response, the workflow moves to GET /me, the commit lands, nothing is enqueued (sinks absent, dispatches 0 — 1/81 and 2/81 feed-wide), nothing inside the app calls it, and a retry rides the claim protocol (_reclaim / _discard_claim / _stamp_completion in .behind.names) — so 'tell them to retry' is safe and no worker hunt is owed. A write added outside that claim silently breaks the replay 24 ops rely on; the ASGI Idempotency middleware that should back it is unmeasured. Empty channels must draw as a closed loop, not a blank.
evidence: fe render chain behind the bridge
workflow step (workflows.js steps[] naming the label)

wells.label: Home
wells.question: Whose is this — which entity owns the door, does everyone agree it lives there, and what sits next to it?
wells.plain: The claim home (c4-graph.js node .slug, the file-claimed registry key every other view is a delta against), the three membership witnesses and their disagreement (.home_ev: file · users · data, verdict), where the alternative entity models would put it (c4.models.homes derived / proposed / seeded), the entity-level coupling around it (l1 edges), and its neighbours by claim, by cluster, or by story.
wells.why: Picks the one panel to open next, tells a newcomer whether the folder is the truth, and after a change whether it still belongs: file says auth, the one caller says auth, but data leans settings (10 vs auth 9 of 24 witnesses), the derived view homes it to d:household_format_preferences (a 6-endpoint cluster with GET /me, GET /settings, PATCH /settings/*), and one more settings write tips the majority. Verdict STAY — the file wins; 29/81 carry a disagreement, 0 move verdicts feed-wide, nothing re-homes. By claim it has 3 siblings (auth is 4/81), by story its neighbours are POST /consent and GET /me.

wells.label: Change pressure
wells.question: Is anyone touching this right now, at which lifecycle stage, and when did it last move — and if not this file, which of the entities it reaches into moved instead?
wells.plain: Recent commits that touched the endpoint (commits.js touched[] naming the id — 30 commits, 2026-07-28 → 2026-08-07), a change in flight on its file with its stage (sim.data.js GABE_SIM touched / pieces / blast), and the reserved levels.json pressure block ({} feed-wide).
wells.why: Sets merge risk before the edit, who to tell after it, and in an incident whether a half-shipped change is the cause: 0 of 30 commits, apps/api/api/setup.py absent from the sim's 28 touched files, every pieces[] empty — at rest. Thin by construction: 59/81 endpoints show no commit and 0/81 are reachable from the seeded sim, so stillness must read as 'no captured change in an 11-day window', not 'stable' — a trail that ends at the window edge, not at zero; the redirect is to commits on settings / allergen / pantry / legal-consent, the entities the chain writes.
evidence: commit touch (commits.js touched[] naming the id)

wells.label: Live traffic
wells.question: Is it failing right now — for one user or everyone, since when, how slow, how often is it called, and what did it return?
wells.plain: The runtime half of an endpoint: latency, throughput, error rate, request volume, timeouts, retries, payload sizes, production callers. The feed is a static map and carries none of it for any endpoint (coverage_note) — no file, no key.
wells.why: The first decision of any incident — severity, page or watch — and the operator's and preattentive lenses both name its absence beside their own wells. It must be DRAWN as an unmeasured state (a hollow gauge that never fills, a still marker that says 'no signal') so a reader never mistakes a quiet map for a quiet system; it is the landing pad if a runtime feed is ever wired in.

verdicts.reason: Every drawn_from key is live on the bench and recounts: c4-graph.js l2.auth.nodes[POST /setup/complete].access.ops = 24 (13 r + 11 w) over 13 models, read-only = Membership + ConsentRecord; owners via l2 model nodes / cross_edges.to_slug = auth 5 (Household, IdempotencyKey, Membership, SetupCompletionState, SubscriptionEntitlement) · settings 5 · allergen 1 (UserDietaryProfile) · pantry 1 (Location) · legal-consent 1 (ConsentRecord); access.commits true; access.sinks absent (only POST /cooking/sessions/{session_id}/complete carries ['queue']); c4.colors carries all five entity hues; the hover count recounts on l2 edges (source/target) + cross_edges (from/to): 30 other endpoints read / 6 write those 11 tables. Feed-wide states match: commits false 28, absent 2. Empty-state rules (thin GREY baseline at 0 ops, dashed at commits false, HATCHED at commits absent) are honest. One naming error: the empty state says 0 ops = 'BOOT lifespan, GET /healthz', but endpoint:BOOT lifespan carries 61 ops; the two 0-ops endpoints are GET /healthz and POST /account/export (the same pair with commits absent).
verdicts.fix: In empty_state replace '0 ops (2/81: BOOT lifespan, GET /healthz)' with '0 ops (2/81: GET /healthz, POST /account/export)'.

verdicts.reason: Ground = c4.colors and tile fill = 0xe5484d both reuse a station channel WITH its station meaning (hull entity hue L1258; 'red is the ACCESS write wire' L2186) — fine. What collides: (1) the WRITE phase makes 11 red tiles PULSE, and the station's only red pulse is the ENC.pulse god dot, drawn in the same hex #e5484d at L1832; (2) the baseline dashed = 'staged, never landed' mints a third dash meaning on top of field dash = kind (CONN.style L1704) and card dash = inferred (.cinf .pchip L248); (3) the door is a ring — GLYPH.endpoint (L1081) is a bolt and a ring on this console is the HL focus ring (L2609–2627). Motion: the READ → WRITE → COMMIT rail is a canonical transaction shape the encoding itself admits is not a measured order, and 13 tiles thickening/pulsing plus the bead, rail and baseline blow through the ≤4–5 moving-objects cap. Glance overclaims: 'thirteen tiles, eleven red' needs counting; only 'mostly red, spills onto four grounds' is pre-attentive.
verdicts.fix: Door = GLYPH.endpoint bolt. WRITE phase = tiles FILL in place as the bead passes under their ground (luminance, one mover, no pulse). commits false = thin GREY baseline (the four-state grey), never dashed. Glance line → 'mostly red, spilling onto four foreign grounds, one solid line under all of it'.

verdicts.reason: Complete at frame zero: 13 tiles with read/write texture, the solid baseline, the dashed sink outline, the rail and both labels are all base-state marks. The head's animations are overlays on resting values — `.t{stroke-width:1}` is the read tile's rest and `rf` thickens from it, `.w{fill:#e5484d;fill-opacity:.85}` is the write tile's rest and the pulse rides on it, the bead is `animation:mv 6s linear infinite` on its own element. encodings.static: Left: the body plug (schema-tinted rounded rect) with seven pins stacked — the first plain (household_name: str), six compound (HouseholdFormatInput, UserFormatInput, DietaryProfileInput, ExplorationPreferencesInput, PrivacyPermissionsInput, NotificationPreferencesInput). A dashed arrow to the door ring, a dashed arrow on to the consumer box (complete_setup) which carries the whole-plug silhouette inside it. Six solid arrows fan from the consumer to six taker boxes (_upsert_*), each wearing one compound pin. Four rail cells at the bottom: ASSEMBLE · DOOR · CONSUME · SPLIT.
encodings.motion: 7 s cycle. ASSEMBLE: the seven pins brighten top to bottom, one every 0.15 s — the count growing is the body being filled. DOOR: a hollow bead (hollow = on an inferred hop) leaves the plug, crosses the door and reaches the consumer along the dashed wires. SPLIT: six filled beads leave the consumer 0.14 s apart, one per solid wire, and each taker's outline thickens on arrival — six functions each receiving their own part. The rail cell lit says which phase is NOW. Reduced motion: beads hidden, SPLIT cell lit, every taker at rest.
encodings.glance: Seven things to assemble, six of them structured; the door does not read the body — the box two hops right does, and splits it six ways.
encodings.still_reads: Field names and types (hover per pin); that 'touches' never says request vs response, so the plug is gsig-inferred (35/81 carry 'body:'); that levels.schema_edges carry no conf field (their solid wires mean 'no doubt recorded', not 'proven'); that household_name has no taker of its own (hover on the consumer); the clipped gsig past its ellipsis.
drawn_from: nests (schema → schema, one hop off the endpoint's schemas) (6)
handler chain (direct out-edges) — calls complete_setup conf inferred
encodings.empty_state: No 'body:' in gsig (46/81) → the plug slot draws as an empty socket outline — BLANK, the wrong question for a GET — and the ASSEMBLE cell is struck through. gsig clipped before the body → the socket HATCHED (never seen). nests 0 → plain pins only. A consumes edge present (1/81: PATCH /settings/exploration) → the plug → door wire turns solid. No schema_edge consumer found → the consumer box GREY with '?' on hover and no fan. Takers 0 → the consumer stands alone at the right and SPLIT is struck.

verdicts.reason: The bench numbers are real: c4-graph.js l2.auth schema:SetupCompleteRequest det.cols = 7 (household_name str + 6 Input types), nests = 6 (5 intra + ExplorationPreferencesInput → settings), levels.json schema_edges carries exactly the six 'takes' edges named (_upsert_dietary ← DietaryProfileInput … _upsert_user_format ← UserFormatInput) plus complete_setup uses SetupCompleteRequest; fn_edges: setup_complete → complete_setup conf inferred, complete_setup has 15 callees with the six _upsert takers conf extracted; consumes = 1 edge feed-wide (PATCH /settings/exploration) vs stats.consumes 70. But the plug is keyed on the literal `body:` in det.gsig, and that literal appears in only 6/81 gsigs (setup/complete, consent, recipes/demand, the three settings PATCHes); 24 more endpoints carry their body as `payload: <Schema>` (30/81 have a schema-typed param). Under the encoding's own empty-state rule ('No body: in gsig → empty socket = BLANK, the wrong question') 24 POST/PATCH/PUT doors with a real request body would be drawn as if a body were the wrong question — a lie on 24/81. The stated 46/81 count does not exist under either rule (75/81 lack the literal; 51/81 lack a schema-typed param).
verdicts.fix: Detect the body by TYPE, not name: the first gsig param (excluding Request/Annotated/Response/scalars) whose annotation names a `schema:` node in c4 l2 — 30/81 light, 51/81 BLANK; restate the empty-state count to 51/81 and keep BLANK only where the method is GET/DELETE and no schema-typed param exists.

verdicts.reason: The plug is tinted KINDCOL.schema #06b6d4, and on an ENDPOINT console that exact hex is the delivery:stream badge (__BADGE_COL.delivery.stream L4232) — a cyan body beside the door reads 'stream' on the one kind where that badge lives. Dashed wire = inferred matches the card law (L247/L248) — good — and the hollow/filled bead riding trust is consistent with opacity = trust. But the ASSEMBLE phase (pins brighten in declaration order, 0.15 s apart) has no upstream cause — a client posts one body — so it is field-order decoration, and with 7 pins + 6 fan beads the cycle exceeds the concurrent-channel cap. The door ring collides with the station's focus ring (GLYPH.endpoint is a bolt, L1081). Glance: '6 takers' and 'the box two hops right reads it' are pre-attentive (fan shape + matching silhouette in the consumer box); 'seven things' is not subitizable.
verdicts.fix: Plug carries the GLYPH.schema braces in currentColor (no cyan fill). Cut the ASSEMBLE phase — pins lit at frame zero; the only motion is body → consumer → six takers. Door = bolt glyph.

verdicts.reason: The head pins the build-up: `.pin{fill:currentColor;fill-opacity:.35}` is the resting state and `.p1{animation:af 7s infinite}.p2{… .15s}…` brighten FROM it — so the plug's seven pins rest DIM, every 7 s loop resets them to dim (no fill-mode), and the takers 'thicken on arrival' the same way. Under prefers-reduced-motion or a Paused cog at t=0 the body reads unassembled and the fan un-received — a start state, the exact thing H4 forbids; the claim 'SPLIT cell lit, every taker at rest' cannot hold while the pins' base is .35.
verdicts.fix: Flip the base: `.pin` at its lit fill-opacity and taker outlines at their thick weight as the resting state; make ASSEMBLE an opacity-0 overlay (a highlight ring travelling down the seven pins) and SPLIT arrival an opacity-0 flash on each taker, so pausing or `animation:none` leaves the full plug, the consumer and six received takers.

encodings.name: The exit fork — one trunk, a gate diamond, the handler's fan of status exits, each chip drawn in its evidence state (adapts Decision fork + belt-lanes + the four availability states + Command trace replay)
channels: position — the trunk runs left → right in request order: door → gate diamond → handler → declared success; every failure exit drops DOWN from the stage that raises it; ambiguous and unnamed cases sit in a tail bin past the fan
size — branch thickness = cases naming that exit (400: 1 · 409: 1 · 422: 2); the trunk beyond the handler carries the most mass (the defining edge: det.status + 2 cases)

count — tick marks under each chip = the cases naming it; the tail bin carries the unnamed count
orientation — an arrowhead on every exit and on the trunk's end
motion — six beads replay the door-scoped status-named cases in C-id order, each leaving the trunk at its exit; a six-cell rail is the NOW cursor
encodings.static: Door ring → thin trunk → gate diamond (get_auth_context) → handler box → a thick trunk with an arrowhead into the LIT '200' chip (two ticks). Under the diamond a dashed drop to a HATCHED '401' chip. Under the handler three arrowed drops to LIT chips 400 (one tick), 409 (one tick), 422 (two ticks, thicker branch). Past them a dashed-grey '404' chip (journey-named) and a grey '·18' chip (no status in the name). Bottom-left a grey page glyph (no docstring). Six empty rail cells along the bottom.
encodings.motion: 9 s cycle. Bead k is the k-th test_setup_complete_* case carrying a status in its name: C1048 → 400, C1051 → 422, C1052 → 422, C1055 → 409, C1056 → 200, C1057 → 200. Each bead runs the trunk from the door, passes the gate (no bead ever drops at 401 — nothing in the feed proves that branch), and turns down at its exit or runs to 200; the chip it lands on brightens. The rail cell that is lit says which case is running. What the change means: each landing is one branch a test proved; a chip nothing lands on all cycle is a branch nobody has proved. Reduced motion: beads hidden, sixth cell lit, every proven chip at rest.
encodings.glance: Four proven exits (400 · 409 · 422 twice · 200 twice), the 401 under the gate hatched — nobody measured it — and a grey page: no docstring.
encodings.still_reads: What each status means for a caller (the case name on hover: missing_key, blank_name, too_many_allergens, without_consent); that the three handler exits are ordered numerically — a display convention, the feed carries no raise order; that the two 404 tokens ride journey cases (C605, C705) and belong to some other step; that the gate CAN refuse (gate:true) though no test or doc names 401 here; the 18 unnamed cases.

encodings.motion: A horizontal cursor with a faint band starts on the handler strip and steps down one layer every 0.7 s — five beats for five layers, so a deeper endpoint takes visibly longer to reach the floor (time = depth; the stream contrast at depth 6 runs one beat longer). encodings.glance: A small door with a wide fan under it: the second row is the long one and it is where the red is — the writes are one hop down, most of the guessed cells sit on its left, and the tree bottoms out at the p95 notch.

verdicts.reason: All numbers recount: c4 behind {fns 29, depth 5, names 12, names_more 17, truncated absent}; det.sig.lines 21 / det.flines 254; levels.json fn_nodes handler {role caller, d2w 1, god false, hub.usage 1}, complete_setup {role accessor, d2w 0, god true, hub.usage 7}; BFS over calls+depends from the handler = layers [3,16,5,1] (25), inferred per layer [1,5,2,0], writers by access.ops rw:w [0,10,2,1]; calls-only [2,15,4,1] (22); L1 = _me_response_from_result (extracted) · get_auth_context (depends, extracted) · complete_setup (inferred, the only fanning cell); ghost row 29 − 25 = 4; MAXES {behind:30, depth:5} at gabe-universe.html:1398. Two labels are wrong but drawn values are not: 'p95 notch' — MAXES.depth is a hand-set station cap (feed depth range 0–7), not a percentile; and '(handler d2w 1)' as the reason the burst lands on L2 — d2w 1 would place the write at L1 where writers = 0 (complete_setup carries d2w 0 with a read-only op, so d2w is not access.ops rw:w).
verdicts.fix: Rename the notch 'station cap (MAXES.depth 5)'; drive the red burst from writers[] (first layer > 0) and drop the d2w citation.

verdicts.reason: Dashed cell = inferred hop and dotted ghost = unreached both match the card law (.cinf .pchip L248, .st-unknown L242); the 2-px #e5484d underline reuses access red with its station meaning; cursor-per-layer is causal (a callee runs after its caller). The collision is the write mark: a RED RING that BURSTS at L2 is ring + pulse + #e5484d — exactly the station's ENC.pulse god dot (L1832, same hex) and HL ring pulse — and on this bench the L1 cell it fires beside (complete_setup) IS god:true in levels.json, so the burst reads as the god mark. Secondary: the rail's 'p95 notch' is MAXES.depth 5 / MAXES.behind 30 — cap constants, not a percentile — a measured-sounding term for a calibration value. Glance ('second row is long and red') is length + hue, pre-attentive.
verdicts.fix: The write mark flashes by luminance in place — the red underlines brighten as the cursor crosses L2, no ring, no burst. Rename the notch to what it is: 'scale max 5 / 30'.

encodings.glance: A long green row, a shorter striped row, an empty third row — guarded on the api side, guarded but untargetable on the web side, nothing end-to-end; and six long walks fan under it, the longest crossing five territories.
